part.text:
All 12 test cases pass. I implemented the solution in `dominoes.go` without touching the test files or adding new files.

## What I did

The spec (`.docs/instructions.md`) asks for a **closed** domino chain: order a set of dominoes so adjacent halves match and the two open ends (first and last halves) match each other. Each stone is used once and may be flipped.

In `dominoes.go` I added:

- **`Domino` type** — `[2]int`, matching how the tests construct and compare dominoes.
- **`MakeChain`** — returns an ordered `[]Domino` and `bool`. Empty input yields an empty chain (`true`). Otherwise it runs a quick feasibility check, then backtracking search.
- **`canChain`** — a necessary-condition filter: every value must appear an even number of times and the stones must form a single connected component. This makes the "can't be chained" and "disconnected" cases fail fast instead of exploring the whole search tree. (Even degree + connectivity is *not* sufficient — the tests explicitly guard against using it as the sole criterion — so the backtracking search still does the real work.)
- **`search`** — backtracking over unused dominoes in both orientations, tracking the current open end value, and only accepting a complete chain whose last half matches the first half.

The single-domino cases work naturally: only a double (`{1,1}`) closes on itself, so `{1,1}` chains but `{1,2}` does not.

I left `dominoes_test.go` and `cases_test.go` untouched.
